articles.title: ‘I get lost going to the bathroom’: John Hannah on world travel, stealing props and being ‘the Scottish Eminem’
articles.summary: The Four Weddings and a Funeral actor answers your questions on being confused with James Nesbitt, his own Sliding Doors moment and a new perspective since turning 60. How often do you get asked to recite that WH Auden poem from Four Weddings and a Funeral, and can you do it from memory right now?
body: In Steve Coogan ’s Paul Calf’s Video Diary, your character praises Orson Welles’ The Trial for its “tremendous energy”, while Paul says he would “rather watch Dave Lee Travis playing Macbeth”. What’s your actual opinion of The Trial [by Franz Kafka]? AdrianH1 God, it’s a long time since I’ve read that. I read a lot of those books in my younger days, but probably, like a lot of people, even those who are graduates of English literature, I’d be hard pushed these days to tell you what it was about, other than the persecution of some minor character.

As a popular jobbing actor, you have a massive list of credits. Has anyone ever come up to you to express their appreciation for a certain role and you had no idea what they were on about? Kevcoe No. It’s always heartwarming when somebody comes up and offers their congratulations on something a little bit lower down the pecking order. Fortunately, people rarely ever come up to tell me that they thought I was shit in something. I quite often get Paul Calf’s Video Diary, and that Macbeth line. To be frank, I can’t quite remember the context.

articles.title: Tom Hiddleston Recalls Trekking to Everest for ‘Tenzing’ and Kevin Feige Telling Him ‘Thor’ Wasn’t ‘Going to Be the Only Film’ He Would Play Loki In
articles.summary: British actor Tom Hiddleston has a privileged view and understanding of the Marvel Cinematic Universe phenomenon, having starred as Loki in “Thor,” only the second film of a now ever-expanding franchise.
body: “We were immediately bonded,” he added. “It was a shared excitement about being invited to make a film like this. Marvel Studios had made one film at that time, which was ‘Iron Man,’ which we both loved, and we were being directed by Kenneth Branagh, Anthony Hopkins was playing our father, Rene Russo was playing our mother, and we had extraordinary resources. We had an amazing, brilliant creative stunt department where we would train for sequences of dizzying choreography. We both loved movement and these opportunities.”

Of the project’s scale, Hiddleston said, “It was a different dimension.” “The scenes themselves were very deep. They were full of turbulence, turmoil, soul and emotion The material was really deep, so the combination of those things was a thrill.”

The Brit thanked late screenwriter Don Payne for developing Loki’s “complex” backstory, and recalled an early conversation with Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige, who told him “Thor” wasn’t “the only film you’re going to be in.”

articles.title: Canada’s Oscar Entry, Berlin Prizewinner ‘Nina Roza’ Acquired in U.S. by Dekanalog (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: New York-based indie distributor Dekanalog has acquired the U.S. rights to “Nina Roza,” Canada’s Academy Awards submission. Geneviève Dulude-De Celles’ film won the Silver Bear for best screenplay at the Berlin Film Festival this year.
body: Dekanalog will release “Nina Roza” theatrically in early 2027, followed by VOD and Blu-ray debuts. The company has also acquired the U.S. rights to Dulude-De Celles’ 2018 feature, “A Colony,” and plans to also release next year.

“ ‘Nina Roza’ brilliantly explores the subtle, but profound ways immigration affects a person’s identity — something all too rarely depicted on screen,” says Sam Wunderl, partner at Dekanalog. “We are incredibly proud to be bringing Dulude-De Celles’s work to a U.S. audience.”

Dulude-De Celles said, “I am thrilled that ‘Nina Roza’ has the opportunity to be presented in the United States. By following the journey of a Canadian of Bulgarian origin who returns to his home country, the film invites us to look with empathy at those who choose to settle far from their homeland. I hope the film will spark discussions about identity, heritage, and the long-term cost of immigration. Our team feels in good hands with Dekanalog and is excited about the next steps in our collaboration.”

articles.title: Global release announced for acclaimed Gaza documentary NAZA
articles.summary: Theatrical rollout across 56 territories planned for documentary about Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza before film will stream on Guardian website. NAZA, the award-winning documentary from Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, is set to be released in cinemas in more than 50…
body: The film, which the Guardian produced, premiered at the Venice film festival earlier this month, where it was met with a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record. The documentary went on to win the special jury prize.

After screenings in Bologna and at the San Sebastián film festival, the film will receive its North American premiere on Saturday at the New York film festival before opening four days later at the IFC Center in New York City. On 9 October it will expand to Los Angeles and other key US cities before a national rollout.

A theatrical release in partnership with MK2 Films is also planned in 55 other territories, including the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Canada, Hong Kong, Brazil, Turkey, Thailand, France, Spain, Germany, Turkey, Central America and the Middle East.
After its run in cinemas, the film will stream in late November on the Guardian’s website, for free, as part of the news organisation’s commitment to the dissemination of independent journalism.

articles.title: Post your questions for Zach Braff
articles.summary: Known to many as JD in Scrubs, Zach Braff has forged a path as a successful writer and director since the release of his acclaimed 2004 indie film Garden State. Now’s your chance to ask him your burning questions.
body: There’s much more to Zach Braff than hospital scrubs and hair that could keep the entire mousse industry afloat. His second career as a film-maker got off to quite the start with his 2004 directorial debut Garden State, which he also wrote and starred in. Shot for just $2.5m, it went on to make more than $35m worldwide, pick up over three dozen award nominations and earn Braff a Grammy for compiling its soundtrack, featuring the Shins, Coldplay and Nick Drake.

Then as a film actor he has also popped up in everything from 2000 gay ensemble comedy-drama The Broken Hearts Club, alongside Timothy Olyphant, and 2006 romantic drama The Last Kiss, opposite Jacinda Barrett, to 2006 workplace romcom The Ex, with Jason Bateman, and 2016 John Steinbeck adaptation In Dubious Battle, directed by James Franco.

articles.title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You
articles.summary: Two viewers complained to the BBC over the "gratuitously offensive" comment made during the show.
body: Complaints about the broadcast of a swear word in connection with Victoria Beckham during an episode of BBC One's Have I Got News For You have been upheld, the corporation's executive complaints unit (ECU) has ruled.
The show, from 7 November last year, hosted by comic and presenter Katherine Ryan, featured an email allegedly sent by Sir David Beckham in which the word was used.
Ryan told the show's panellists: "I don't know that we are allowed to broadcast the c-word, but you did reference Victoria Beckham earlier and we'll allow that."

Two viewers complained that this was gratuitously offensive, and the BBC said there was no justification for a comment which "presented Victoria Beckham as equivalent to a particularly offensive word".

articles.title: ‘I’m a writer but then nobody’s perfect’: how Billy Wilder conquered Hollywood
articles.summary: From émigré roots to a titan of modern cinema, penning classics such as Double Indemnity, Some Like It Hot and The Apartment, a new retrospective celebrates the father of film noir’s incredible career. Like all survivors, Billy Wilder never forgot where he came from or what he had left behind.
body: Wilder was an inveterate self-mythologiser, a film-maker with a brand long before there were opportunities for promotion through Instagram accounts and chicken shop dates. He told a story of living in Berlin during his fledgling years in show business and being kept awake all night by “a toilet that was on the blink”.
“I would lie there and listen to it, and since I was young and romantic, I’d imagine it was a beautiful waterfall – just to get my mind off the monotony of it and the thought of it being a can.”

Most of us would have called a plumber but the aspiring young film-maker chose instead to use the incident as fuel for perhaps the greatest body of work in cinema’s golden age. This is the man who made Double Indemnity, the archetypal film noir and the genre’s zenith, a film often imitated but never equalled. He was responsible for Some Like It Hot, a movie routinely voted the greatest comedy ever made, while his Sunset Boulevard is generally acknowledged as the best film about show business. The Apartment, arguably his magnum opus, is rightly considered one of the greatest films in the history of the medium.

articles.title: Greek PM urges Burnham to return Elgin Marbles permanently
articles.summary: Andy Burnham said in 2023 the sculptures should be returned to Greece with "no strings attached".
body: The Greek prime minister has called on Andy Burnham to find the "political will" to send the Parthenon sculptures back to Greece.
Kyriakos Mitsotakis wrote in the Guardian that returning the classical treasures, also known as the Elgin Marbles in the UK, would "send a powerful signal" but would require "courage".
The sculptures have been on display in the British Museum since the 19th Century, though Greece has long disputed the legality of their removal.

Mitsotakis and his government have previously held talks with the British Museum about the sculptures, but the two have so far failed to reach an agreement, with Greek authorities seeking their permanent return.

articles.title: Susan Sarandon, Hannah Einbinder Detained at United Nations Netanyahu Protest
articles.summary: Fellow actor Caleb Hearon was also among the nearly 100 demonstrators taken into custody ahead of the Israeli leader addressing the United Nations General Assembly in New York City.
body: Susan Sarandon, Hannah Einbinder and Caleb Hearon on Thursday were reportedly among around 100 protesters taken into custody on Thursday in New York City ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressing the United Nations General Assembly.
Sarandon was detained, according to a number of outlets, including The New York Times, with photographers snapping images of the Oscar winner waiting to be transported from the protest.

And the U.S. edition of The Sun tabloid, while including footage of Sarandon being taken into custody, also posted photos of Hearon and Einbinder being arrested near the UN headquarters. Einbinder recently defended fellow actor Mark Ruffalo against an accusation of “antisemitism” from Paramount Skydance over his opposition to the studio’s deal for Warner Bros. Discovery.

Representatives for Sarandon, Einbinder and Hearon could not be reached for comment on Thursday, and the New York Police Department also could not be contacted via its media phone line. Reports indicate the celebrities and politicians were detained by the NYPD for blocking traffic and roadways along First Avenue near 39th Street, just a few blocks south of the UN headquarters.
points: Fellow actor Caleb Hearon was also among the nearly 100 demonstrators taken into custody ahead of the Israeli leader addressing the United Nations General Assembly in New York City.
